newsitem.title: UK: UK's PIA expects acceleration on mis-selling probe.
newsitem.headline: UK's PIA expects acceleration on mis-selling probe.

text.p: Britain's Personal Investment Authority said it had some 558,000 cases of possible mis-selling of pensions on its books, and 37,000 assesments had been completed.
Collette Bowe, PIA chief executive, told parliament's Treasury Committee 478,000 of those were regarded as priority cases, many of which date back to a scandal in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Some 11,000 offers of redress worth 80 million stg had been made, and 61 million had been accepted, Bowe said.

Responding to criticism from the committee that only one percent of the cases had been dealt with, she said it could not have foressen problems, many of which were due to external factors and the method of reviewing possible mis-selling.

But PIA chairman Joe Palmer said the method had been simplified and he hoped to have much of the backlog out of the way by the end of the year, having called in those parties with many priority cases to find ways to speed up the process.
Bowe said the PIA's priority was to secure adequate financial compensation for mis-selling, rather than on disciplinary action against those involved in mis-selling.

But Palmer said he had informed some players in the industry, which he did not name, that they could face disciplinary proceedings. Bowe said she could not name the parties likely to be the greatest culprits in the mis-selling.
Bowe said the majority of the mis-selling problem was due to incompetence and poor management rather than fraud.
She said a way of ensuring public confidence in the PIA would be to ensure that directors be appointed by the government, and not by the current election by industry members and co-option.
They said it was too early to respond in detail to proposals by the Conservative Party to reform the pension system, through the Pensions Plus scheme announced last week.
